title: Compactification and inseparable preparation of a marked relative curve
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime and let $Y_0$ be an affine integral excellent Noetherian scheme of finite dimension $n$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Let $W$ be an integral affine excellent Noetherian scheme and $f_0:W\to Y_0$ a dominant finite-type morphism whose generic fibre is an integral curve. Let $Z_W\subset W$ be nowhere dense and suppose its generic fibre is zero-dimensional or empty. There are an affine integral normal excellent Noetherian scheme $Y_1$ of dimension at most $n$, finite and dominant over $Y_0$, an integral excellent separated Noetherian scheme $P$, a proper dominant morphism $f:P\to Y_1$, an effective Cartier divisor $E\subset P$, an open subscheme $P^\circ\subset P$, and a proper surjective morphism $h:P^\circ\to W$ finite over a dense open and of generic degree prime to $\ell$. The maps to $Y_0$ commute; $P^\circ$ is dense; and $|E|\cap P^\circ=h^{-1}Z_W$. If $\eta_1$ is the generic point of $Y_1$, then $P_{\eta_1}$ is a smooth geometrically integral curve and $E_{\eta_1}$ is finite etale, possibly empty. The prime $\ell$ is invertible on all these schemes. Normal means having integrally closed local domains. Geometrically integral means integral after every field extension. The divisor $E$ is locally defined by one non-zero-divisor.

Conventions for the notions used here: [def-pc-scheme], [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

source.place: Expose IX 1.3, printed p. 132, from affine compactification through blowup, finite radicial extension, normalization and Stein factorization. Use the reduced marked support after inseparable normalization and blow it up if necessary to retain an effective Cartier marking; on the smooth generic curve its reduced finite etale ideal is already invertible. For geometric normalization and etale residue fields, Stacks Tag 0BXT (varieties-lemma-finite-extension-geometrically-normal) and Tag 030R (algebra-lemma-make-separable).
